calls.title: Aircall + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting addressed plans to expand GrowthBook's usage from basic experiments to full feature flagging, enhancing rollout control and targeting. Current limitations with Ercol's server-side flags prompted this exploration, highlighting the need for advanced features such as gradual rollouts and automatic rollback during errors. The demo will showcase both basic and advanced functionalities, aiming for buy-in from nearly 200 product and engineering employees. Participants expressed strong interest in GrowthBook's new data science features aimed at expediting experiment evaluation and providing deeper insights. Additionally, the team is weighing the benefits of self-hosting versus a SaaS model, considering operational overhead, privacy, and cost factors.
calls.keywords: Feature Flagging, GrowthBook, Safe Rollouts, Role-Based Access, Experimentation, SaaS vs Self-Hosted

calls.title: Aircall + GrowthBook
calls.summary: Aircall is exploring the adoption of a scalable feature flagging and experimentation platform, specifically GrowthBook, to facilitate faster and lower-risk feature deployments. The platform supports granular rollouts and role-based access controls to improve governance across teams. Key functionalities include multi-environment management within a single GrowthBook instance, ensuring project isolation, and monitoring of features. Furthermore, it allows complex targeting options, such as user-specific flags, percentage rollouts, and integration with various data sources for real-time metrics analysis. A new product analytics tool is also being introduced, enabling users to track product health and engagement—currently in beta with regular updates planned to enhance capabilities.
calls.keywords: Feature Flagging, Experimentation, Role-Based Access Control, Safe Rollouts, Data Warehouse Integration, Product Analytics

calls.title: Aircall + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion centered on establishing clear pricing and contract terms to align with Aircall’s budget, highlighting a full user seat price of $1,250 per year and $500 for read-only users. Nestor emphasized clarity in pricing compared to competitors, while Christian provided details on platform fees that cover development and prioritized support. The need for a reliable SaaS solution was discussed due to past reliability issues with in-house systems, aiming to integrate feature flagging and experimentation to enhance adoption and support a culture of experimentation. Leadership engagement was planned to clarify pricing, flexibility in negotiations, and the importance of demonstrating past experimentation impacts to ensure buy-in for future efforts.
calls.keywords: Feature flags, Experimentation, Pricing model, SaaS, Reliability, Negotiation

calls.title: Aircall + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion centered on GrowthBook's pricing proposal for its enterprise offering, which was deemed too high by Aircall's representatives, particularly regarding the $100K annual platform fee and costs for user licenses. Christopher Howard expressed concerns that this cost exceeds their discretionary budget by double, necessitating significant price adjustments for approval. Christian Liebenow suggested a standard 10% discount for collaboration but acknowledged the possibility of exploring more flexible pricing options. Key features of the enterprise offering, such as SSO and role-based access, were highlighted as critical for Aircall. Ongoing innovations, including AI tool integrations, were also discussed for future value. Next steps involve revising the proposal to align better with Aircall's budget constraints.
calls.keywords: feature flagging, pricing proposal, enterprise offering, single sign-on, user permissions, joint marketing
